s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic sinusitis with destruction of nasal structures and recurrent infections
salient_findings: Crusting and irritation of the sinuses
Destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates
Growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas in culture
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
5-year history of recurrent sinus infections
No prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma
Occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
Normal laboratory tests for inflammation and autoimmune markers
Negative HIV test
Substantial septal deformity on CT scans
Thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses
Erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum on Chest CT
Noncaseating granulomas in sinus mucosa
Growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas in culture
Positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node
Positive second FESS AFB PCR probe

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node and second FESS AFB PCR probe

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Noncaseating granulomas in sinus mucosa and normal laboratory tests for inflammation and autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Destruction of nasal structures and recurrent infections, similar to those seen in granulomatosis with polyangiitis

shortlist.label: Midline destructive granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Substantial septal deformity on CT scans and destruction of the sinus septate

shortlist.label: Rhinoscleroma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic sinusitis with destruction of nasal structures and recurrent infections, consistent with rhinoscleroma

raw.rationale: Positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node and second FESS AFB PCR probe, along with noncaseating granulomas in sinus mucosa, are indicative of tuberculosis infection.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can cause noncaseating granulomas, the positive AFB PCR probes point more specifically to tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Normal laboratory tests for inflammation and autoimmune markers, and lack of other systemic symptoms, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Midline destructive granuloma
rejected.why: This condition is more associated with natural killer/T-cell lymphoma or other specific causes not indicated here.

rejected.label: Rhinoscleroma
rejected.why: The presence of noncaseating granulomas and positive AFB PCR probes, rather than the characteristic Mikulicz cells, makes rhinoscleroma less likely.
